SCOPE NARROWED after epic e369's plan-review pass 4 forced the decision earlier than this bug anticipated.

The plan-review gate correctly pointed out that J2 (62d9) CANNOT defer the `deleted` key: J2 unifies the two `adapters/` copies into one dict, and a single dict cannot preserve two callers that currently disagree. So the decision moved INTO J2:

- **J2 now decides it**: the unified map adopts `"deleted": "Done"`. Rationale established while investigating this bug — there are actually THREE copies of the status map, and TWO already agree on `Done` (`outbound_fields._LOCAL_TO_JIRA_STATUS` and `rebar_reconciler/config.py:37`'s `local_to_jira_status`). Only the ACLI-side `jira_fields` copy omits the key, falling through to `status.replace("_", " ").title()` -> `"Deleted"`, which is NOT a state in the live DIG workflow ({To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done}) — so Jira would reject that transition. `"Deleted"` is a latent bug, not behavior worth preserving. `deleted` is a real `TicketStatus` (src/rebar/types.py:21), so the path is reachable.

**What REMAINS in this bug:**
1. The missing ACLI-side characterization pins — the original finding. The ACLI status/priority resolution has no oracle, which is exactly why my mutation of `jira_fields._LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` left the suite 30/30 GREEN. J2 adds a pin for the `deleted` value it changes, but broad ACLI-path coverage is still absent.
2. Folding `config.py:37`'s THIRD copy into the single `jira_family` definition. Deliberately out of epic e369's scope: its call sites are engine-level config with a wider blast radius than the adapter seam.

So after J2 lands, 'exactly one dict literal' holds within `adapters/`, but `config.py` still carries its own. This bug closes that last gap and adds the missing oracle.

IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1186 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1186), commit
e62afec98e, based on main 46dae1a5aa.

=== WHAT THIS TICKET TURNED OUT TO BE ===
Its ORIGINAL scope — two drifted copies of the local->Jira maps inside `adapters/jira/` — was
already delivered by story J2 [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743], verified against the tree rather than
assumed: `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` is now the sole adapter-side definition, the ACLI
transport reads it (`acli.py:73,75`; `acli_cli_ops.py:35`) and so does the Backend port
(`outbound_fields.py:35-36`), and the `deleted` drift is decided (`"Done"`) and pinned by
`test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py`. Three of the four original ACs were met.
The residue is the THIRD copy, which J2 deliberately left out of scope and named this ticket for
in its own module docstring: "``rebar_reconciler/config.py``'s separate third copy is deliberately
out of this story's scope — see bug fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61." The plan was rewritten to that residue
before review, and PASSED FIRST TRY.

=== THE GAP, MEASURED ===
`config.local_to_jira_status` is content-identical to `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` today (compared
programmatically: `==` is True), so there is no drift YET. Nothing prevented one. Mutating
`config.local_to_jira_status["deleted"]` to `"Archived-MUTANT"` — not a state in the live DIG
workflow — left **59 tests GREEN** across `state/test_config.py`,
`test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py`, `test_jira_family_seam.py` and
`test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py`.

=== THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS A TEST RATHER THAN AN IMPORT ===
A parity test plus a lock-step comment — NOT single-sourcing via an import. `config.py` imports
nothing but `__future__`, and `adapters/jira_family` declares a one-way dependency direction
("concrete backends import this package; it never imports them back"), so importing the adapter
into core would invert that layering and put the operator-override surface — including the
documented empty-dict kill-switch — behind an adapter import.
This is the idiom the file ALREADY uses for the same problem one map over:
`config.jira_to_local_status` is a second literal of `inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS`, kept
honest by `test_jira_to_local_status_parity_with_inbound_differ` plus a comment saying so. The new
test mirrors it, and the new comment mirrors that comment's form.

=== AC-BY-AC ===
[full-dict equality via a by-path load] `test_local_to_jira_status_parity_with_the_jira_family_map`
asserts `config.local_to_jira_status == value_maps.LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`. Full dict, not a spot
check — the existing idea-across-all-maps test already pins ONE key (`idea`), and the other six
were the unguarded ones, which is why the mutation went unseen.
[MUTATION-CHECKED, both verdicts] With `"deleted"` mutated: **1 failed, 59 passed** — the new test
fails naming the drift, and it is the ONLY failure. Reverted: **60 passed**.
[lock-step comment naming the canonical map and the enforcing test] Added above
`local_to_jira_status`, in the same form as the existing `jira_to_local_status` comment.
[config.py still imports nothing outside `__future__`] Verified: `grep '^import\|^from'` returns
only `from __future__ import annotations`.
[kill-switch and override unchanged; only an ADDED test] `git diff --numstat`: test_config.py
53 added / 0 deleted; config.py 12 added / 0 deleted. Zero deleted lines in either file, so no
existing test was edited and no behaviour changed — the change is a comment and a test.
[all four suites pass] 60 passed.

=== NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY ===
No map VALUES changed (they already agree; changing one would be a behaviour change this ticket
does not need), and the priority map is untouched because `config.py` has NO priority copy —
verified: the module exposes no priority attribute at all, so there is no third priority literal
to pin.

GATES: `make lint` and `make typecheck` both pass. Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

# Pin `config.local_to_jira_status` against the canonical Jira-family map

## Context / Problem

**This ticket's original scope is already delivered; what remains is one specific residue, and this
plan has been rewritten to that residue.** Filed during J1 as "the local->Jira maps exist in two
drifted copies inside `adapters/jira/`". Story J2 [rebar:62d9-9f6d-ecf4-4743] consolidated those two
into a single definition and resolved the drift. Verified against the tree, not assumed:

* `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` now holds the SOLE adapter-side definition
  (`LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA`, `LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA`).
* The ACLI transport reads it (`acli.py:73,75`; `acli_cli_ops.py:35`) and so does the Backend port
  (`outbound_fields.py:35-36`), both via an alias to the old private names.
* The `deleted` drift is decided: the unified map adopts `"deleted": "Done"`, and
  `test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py` pins it
  (`test_deleted_now_resolves_to_done_instead_of_the_invalid_deleted`).

So original ACs 1-3 are met. The residue is the **THIRD copy**, which J2 deliberately left out of its
scope and named this ticket for, in `value_maps.py`'s own module docstring: "``rebar_reconciler/
config.py``'s separate third copy is deliberately out of this story's scope — see bug
fe15-3bc4-ed70-4b61."

## Evidence — the residue is a REAL unpinned gap, measured

`config.local_to_jira_status` (`config.py:24-38`) is a key-for-key **independent literal**.
Today it is content-identical to `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` (compared programmatically: `==` is True), so
there is no drift *yet* — but nothing prevents one.

MUTATION EXPERIMENT (the same method that originally exposed this bug class): setting
`config.local_to_jira_status["deleted"] = "Archived-MUTANT"` — a value that is NOT a state in the live
DIG workflow ({To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done}) — left **59 passed, 0 failed** across
`state/test_config.py`, `test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py`, `test_jira_family_seam.py`, and
`test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py`. Nothing catches divergence. That is precisely the failure mode
this ticket reported, surviving in the one copy J2 did not touch.

Note the partial existing cover, so this plan does not re-add it: `test_config.py`'s
`test_idea_maps_to_jira_idea_across_all_status_maps` already pins the `idea -> IDEA` entry across all
three maps. It is ONE key. The other six are unpinned, which is why the mutation above went unseen.

## Approach — a parity test, NOT a shared import

**Do not make `config.py` import the canonical map.** `config.py` currently imports nothing but
`__future__` — it is a deliberately zero-dependency core module — and `adapters/jira_family/` is a
VENDOR package whose `__init__` states its dependency direction is one-way ("Concrete backends import
this package; it never imports them back"). Having core `config` import a Jira adapter would invert
that layering. It would also put the operator-override surface and the documented empty-dict
kill-switch (`test_config.py:91-98`) behind an adapter import.

**Use the idiom this file already established for exactly this problem.** `config.jira_to_local_status`
is a second literal of `inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS`, and the codebase keeps the two honest
with a PARITY TEST plus a lock-step comment — see the comment at `config.py:50-51` ("Must stay in
lock-step with inbound_differ._JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS (parity is enforced by tests/.../test_config.py)")
and `test_jira_to_local_status_parity_with_inbound_differ`. Mirror that, one layer over.

`test_config.py` already has the mechanism: `_load_attr(module_file, attr)` loads a constant **from a
file path** via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, so the test reads the adapter's map WITHOUT
importing the adapter package into core's test context — and it is already called with
`"adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py"` today. No new machinery is needed.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_config.py` — ONE new parity test.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/config.py` — a lock-step COMMENT above
  `local_to_jira_status`, mirroring the one already above `jira_to_local_status`. No code change.

**NOT in scope:** any change to a map's VALUES (they already agree; changing one would be a behaviour
change this ticket does not need); any production import between core and the adapter layer; the
priority map (`config.py` has NO priority copy — verified: no priority attribute exists on the module,
so there is no third priority literal to pin).

## Testing

The oracle is the parity test itself, and it must be shown to have teeth rather than asserted to:
re-run the mutation above and confirm the new test goes RED, then revert and confirm GREEN. A parity
test that passes against a divergent map is worse than none.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a test in `state/test_config.py` asserts `config.local_to_jira_status` equals
      `LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA` loaded from `adapters/jira_family/value_maps.py` via the existing
      `_load_attr` helper — full-dict equality, not a per-key spot check
- [ ] MUTATION-CHECKED: with `config.local_to_jira_status["deleted"]` changed to a non-workflow value
      the new test FAILS, and with it reverted the test PASSES; both verdicts recorded on this ticket
- [ ] `config.py` carries a lock-step comment naming the canonical map and the enforcing test, in the
      same form as the existing `jira_to_local_status` comment
- [ ] `config.py` still imports nothing outside `__future__` — asserted by reading the diff; no
      production dependency from core onto `adapters/`
- [ ] the empty-dict kill-switch and operator-override behaviour are unchanged — the existing
      `test_config.py` suite passes with ZERO edits to its existing tests (`git diff` shows only an
      ADDED test)
- [ ] `state/test_config.py`, `test_acli_status_resolution_heldout.py`, `test_jira_family_seam.py`
      and `test_jira_family_boundary_heldout.py` all pass
